name: msdoc_read_excel
description:
Reads cell values from one worksheet of an Excel workbook (.xlsx/.xlsm, via openpyxl). Files are looked up by name in the docs folder (data/msdocs; msdoc_list_files shows it).
Returns {filename, sheet_name, data, row_count, column_count}: data is a list of rows, each a list of cell values; with include_formulas also formulas, [{cell, formula}] per row.
Inputs (* required): filename*, sheet_name (wins over sheet_index), sheet_index (0-based), max_rows (1-10000; default 100), include_formulas (default false; when true data holds cell objects rather than values, so use the formulas list). Without a sheet the active sheet is read. Legacy .xls cannot be read.
For sheet names use msdoc_get_excel_sheets; msdoc_read_excel_sheet is the same read without the formula option.
Example: {"filename": "sales.xlsx", "sheet_name": "Q1", "max_rows": 50}

filename.description: Name of the Excel file to read (.xlsx)

sheet_name.description: Name of the sheet to read (optional)

sheet_index.description: Index of the sheet to read, 0-based (optional)

max_rows.description: Maximum number of rows to return

include_formulas.description: Include cell formulas in the output

examples.description: Read first sheet of Excel file
